Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:14:22 -0800
Subject: Spike in latency + 500s — reserved capacity not honoring throughput

Hi Jordan —

We started seeing a sustained increase in request latency at ~07:40 PST and a rising rate of 500s across our inference endpoints. We are on a Reserved capacity plan and were expecting stable throughput (commit: 1200 RPS). Dashboard shows token queueing and requests being throttled back to ~600 RPS. This started impacting checkout flows (user-facing errors).

Attached a small sample of requests and a short tail of the error responses (lexiq-sample-requests.json). Can you confirm whether Redwood is throttling us or if this is a client-side degradation? We need an ETA on mitigation — we’re in the middle of a large processing window.

Sofia Ramirez
Head of Platform
Lexiq

Subject: Re: Spike in latency + 500s — reserved capacity not honoring throughput

Quick triage from ops (initial findings):
- Region: us-west-2 (Lexiq primary traffic).
- Symptom: continuous high queue depth on Lexiq’s reserved allocation starting 07:38 PST. Token-level queueing observed and kernel queue latencies increased.
- Error profile: ~76% 200s, ~18% 500s (backend OOM/kv-cache-miss bursts), remainder timeouts.
- Observed reserved throughput served: ~620 RPS vs committed 1200 RPS.

Attachments: pool-metrics-20261113.csv (sample metrics), incident-snapshot-08-30.png (graph of queue depth).

Immediate remediation options (short list):
1) Emergency burst: allocate additional burst pool capacity in us-west-2 for 90–120 minutes. This is fastest to reduce queueing.
2) Traffic steering: temporarily route a percentage of low-priority traffic to a compatible but lower-cost model variant in another pool.
3) KV/prefix cache warm-up: attempt an aggressive cache priming for hot prefixes to reduce 500s due to cache misses.

I recommend option 1 + 3 for fastest impact. Cost estimate for 2-hour burst attached (proposed-burst-cost-estimate.xlsx).

I’ll start a mitigations runbook and can trigger the burst once we have exec signoff.

Irene Choi
Head of Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Sofia — quick update and next steps from Redwood: 

1) What we did (completed):
- Confirmed reserved pool saturation in us-west-2 and increased burst capacity (authorized by Redwood execs) at 09:05 PST.
- Applied targeted KV cache priming for hot prefixes.
- Shifted ~20% low-priority traffic to a compatible variant to reduce pressure on the reserved pool.

2) Status now:
- Measured throughput served: ~1150 RPS (approximate) and queue depth returning to normal.
- Error rate has dropped to ~2% 500s, latency median back to baseline.

3) Next steps (we’ll follow up in writing):
- Ops will monitor for 2 hours and provide checkpoints at 30/60/90 minutes.
- We will prepare a short exec readout for Vivek at 11:00 PST and a compensation recommendation for your procurement team.

We apologize for the disruption. As a good-faith step we’re proposing a one-time service credit; Marissa will follow up with proposed terms. Please reply if you see any remaining issues.
